title: Contract Pricing Agreement: Reference Price for Closing Out a Discontinued Item
content:
**Reference price for closing out a discontinued Contract Pricing Agreement item**

The close-out price of a discontinued contract item on a Contract Pricing Agreement starts from the following reference, read from the agreement's price claim records and contract item price lines:

1. Where the latest decision recorded on a price claim for the item, dated on or after the effective date of the item's latest price line, records the unit price the agreement sets, the close-out price is that decided price.
2. Where no such decision exists and the item's latest price line is an annual escalation that took effect on one of the 30 days before the discontinuation date, the close-out price is that line's prior unit price.
3. Otherwise it is the contract unit price on the item's latest price line.

Calendar days from one date to another count the later date and not the earlier one. Wherever a latest or most recent record of a kind is taken, it is the one with the latest date, and among records of the same date the one recorded first.

| Latest price line | Decision dated on or after that line's effective date | Close-out price |
|---|---|---|
| Any | Yes, recording a unit price | That decided price |
| Annual escalation effective 1 to 30 days before the discontinuation date | No | The escalation line's prior unit price |
| Annual escalation effective 31 or more days before the discontinuation date, on it, or after it | No | The latest line's contract unit price |
| Any other kind of line | No | The latest line's contract unit price |

Hypothetical example: an escalation from 9.8000 to 10.1000 effective 12 days before the discontinuation date, with no decision since: close-out price 9.8000.
